title: Herzliebester Jesu, was hast du verbrochen
note: v6 (chorale-generation, 12 October 2026): as v5, and under a soprano suspension the inner voices leave out its resolution's note (doubling the root or fifth), so it is not heard early (early resolutions 2 of 31, Bach 4 of 67). v5: as v4, and the inner voices move as Bach's do: moving figures restored where the licence allows them (short notes 41%, Bach 40%), suspensions taken where earned (1.6 a hundred notes, Bach 2.1), a step carried across the beat into a scale passage (moves in runs of three steps or more 24%, Bach 24%; v4 16%). v4: as v3, and no voice sounds the resolution of a suspension held in another (early resolutions 4 of 30 suspensions, Bach 4 of 67; v3 10 of 32). v3: as v2 (Bach's own figures beat by beat), but every figure licensed as a counterpoint teacher would check it: each note a chord tone, or a dissonance reached and left by step, or a suspension prepared as a chord tone on the beat before, making a fourth, seventh or ninth over the bass and resolved down by step; notes spelled as the key or the chord spells them (Bach's figure keeps its shape, takes this context's notes); no augmented second, fourth or fifth in a line; anticipations reached by step. Bach's soprano.
